notice: Control references are identifiers only. No standard text is reproduced. Applicability of any framework to a given customer is an assessor decision, not a property of this catalogue.

checks.check_name: Privileged accounts have a strong second factor registered
checks.description: Every account holding a privileged directory role must have a phishing-resistant or app-based authentication method registered. SMS and voice alone do not satisfy this check.
checks.remediation: Register FIDO2 keys or Microsoft Authenticator for each privileged account, then remove the weak methods. Enforce with a Conditional Access policy scoped to directory roles.

checks.check_name: All enabled accounts have MFA registered
checks.description: Every enabled member account must have at least one second factor registered.
checks.remediation: Run an MFA registration campaign, then enforce registration through a Conditional Access policy before the grace period ends.

checks.check_name: No dormant privileged accounts
checks.description: A privileged account that has not signed in for 90 days is an unmonitored path into the tenant.
checks.remediation: Remove the role assignment or disable the account. Where standing access is genuinely required, move it to Privileged Identity Management with time-bound activation.

checks.check_name: No dormant enabled standard accounts
checks.description: Enabled accounts with no sign-in for 180 days should be disabled as part of the access review cycle.
checks.remediation: Confirm with the account owner's line manager, then disable rather than delete so audit history is preserved.

checks.check_name: Global Administrator count is within a defensible range
checks.description: Fewer than two Global Administrators leaves no break-glass path; more than five is an uncontrolled blast radius. Both fail.
checks.remediation: Target two to four permanent Global Administrators, with one cloud-only break-glass account excluded from Conditional Access and monitored for use.

checks.check_name: Legacy authentication is blocked
checks.description: Legacy authentication protocols bypass Conditional Access and MFA entirely. A tenant that has not blocked them has no effective MFA regardless of registration coverage.
checks.remediation: Create a Conditional Access policy blocking Exchange ActiveSync and other legacy clients. Review sign-in logs for legacy usage before enforcing.

checks.check_name: Conditional Access enforces MFA for privileged roles
checks.description: Registration is not enforcement. An enabled Conditional Access policy must require MFA for directory role holders.
checks.remediation: Create an enabled policy targeting directory roles with the MFA grant control, excluding only the break-glass account.

checks.check_name: At least one Conditional Access policy is enabled
checks.description: Policies left in report-only mode provide telemetry, not control.
checks.remediation: Move validated report-only policies into enabled state after reviewing their impact reports.

checks.check_name: Standard users cannot register applications
checks.description: Self-service app registration lets any user create a service principal and consent path into tenant data.
checks.remediation: Set the default user role permission for application creation to No, and route requests through an approval process.

checks.check_name: Guest invitations are restricted
checks.description: Unrestricted guest invitation allows any member to grant an external identity access to tenant resources.
checks.remediation: Set guest invite restrictions so only administrators and users in the Guest Inviter role may invite.

checks.check_name: No application credentials have expired
checks.description: An expired app secret means either a broken integration nobody noticed or a credential that was silently replaced without decommissioning the old registration.
checks.remediation: Review each application with an expired credential, remove the registration if unused, and rotate to certificate-based authentication where the integration is still required.

checks.check_name: Application credentials expire within 12 months
checks.description: Multi-year app secrets outlive the staff who created them and the change record that justified them.
checks.remediation: Cap credential lifetime at 12 months in the app registration policy and automate rotation.

checks.check_name: Directory synchronisation state is known
checks.description: Hybrid identity changes the authoritative source for account lifecycle. The assessment must record which it is.
checks.remediation: Record the identity architecture in the assessment scope and confirm which directory owns joiner-mover-leaver.

checks.check_name: Managed devices report as compliant
checks.description: Devices enrolled in Intune must evaluate as compliant against an assigned compliance policy.
checks.remediation: Triage non-compliant devices by reason. Most resolve to missing encryption, an out-of-date OS, or a stale check-in.

checks.check_name: Managed devices have disk encryption enabled
checks.description: Full-disk encryption on every managed endpoint. This is the control that determines whether a lost laptop is an incident or a notification.
checks.remediation: Deploy BitLocker or FileVault through an Intune configuration profile with silent enablement and key escrow to Entra ID.

checks.check_name: No jailbroken or rooted devices are enrolled
checks.description: A rooted device cannot enforce any policy applied to it.
checks.remediation: Block jailbroken devices in the compliance policy with immediate action, and wipe corporate data from the affected devices.

checks.check_name: Managed devices have checked in recently
checks.description: A device that has not synced for 30 days is reporting a stale posture. Its compliance verdict cannot be relied on as current evidence.
checks.remediation: Investigate devices that have stopped checking in. They are usually decommissioned without being retired from Intune.

checks.check_name: At least one device compliance policy is configured
checks.description: Enrolment without a compliance policy produces inventory, not control.
checks.remediation: Create a baseline compliance policy per platform covering encryption, OS minimum version and screen lock.

checks.check_name: Device compliance policies require encryption
checks.description: The compliance policy itself must mandate storage encryption, otherwise compliant status carries no assurance about it.
checks.remediation: Enable the storage encryption requirement in each platform compliance policy.

checks.check_name: Device compliance policies require a passcode
checks.description: A device passcode requirement must be asserted by policy, not assumed from the platform default.
checks.remediation: Enable the password requirement with a minimum length of six in each compliance policy.

checks.check_name: No network security group exposes a sensitive port to the internet
checks.description: Inbound allow rules from any source to management or database ports. This is the highest-yield check in the catalogue and the one most likely to be true on first run.
checks.remediation: Replace the rule with a source restricted to a named IP range, or front the service with Azure Bastion or a private endpoint. Remove the rule entirely where the service is not meant to be reachable.

checks.check_name: No network security group allows unrestricted inbound access
checks.description: Any inbound allow rule whose source is the internet, regardless of port.
checks.remediation: Narrow the source to a defined prefix. Where public exposure is intentional, document it as an accepted risk with a compensating control.

checks.check_name: Storage accounts deny anonymous blob access
checks.description: Allowing public blob access means any container in the account can be made world-readable by anyone with write access to it.
checks.remediation: Set allowBlobPublicAccess to false at the account level. Serve genuinely public content through a CDN with a dedicated account.

checks.check_name: Storage accounts enforce HTTPS-only traffic
checks.description: Data in transit to storage must be encrypted.
checks.remediation: Enable secure transfer required on every storage account. Legacy SMB file share clients are the usual reason this is off.

checks.check_name: Storage accounts require TLS 1.2 or higher
checks.description: TLS 1.0 and 1.1 are deprecated and fail most regulatory baselines.
checks.remediation: Set the minimum TLS version to 1.2 on every storage account.

checks.check_name: Storage account network rules default to deny
checks.description: A storage firewall that defaults to Allow is not a firewall.
checks.remediation: Set the network default action to Deny and add explicit virtual network rules or private endpoints.

checks.check_name: Storage encryption at rest is enabled for blob and file
checks.description: Platform encryption should be on by default; this check confirms it has not been altered.
checks.remediation: Re-enable service encryption. Investigate why it was changed, because it requires a deliberate action.

checks.check_name: Subscription activity logs are exported to durable storage
checks.description: Without an export, activity log retention is 90 days and there is no forensic record beyond it.
checks.remediation: Create a subscription diagnostic setting shipping the activity log to a Log Analytics workspace, with retention set to the contractual or regulatory period.

checks.check_name: Cloud resources carry an ownership tag
checks.description: An untagged resource has no accountable owner, which blocks every remediation workflow that follows.
checks.remediation: Enforce an owner tag through Azure Policy with a deny effect on new resources, and backfill existing ones.

checks.check_name: Storage accounts disable shared key access
checks.description: Shared key access bypasses Entra ID authentication and role-based access control entirely, and the key cannot be attributed to a user.
checks.remediation: Disable shared key authorisation and move clients to Entra ID authentication with managed identities.

checks.check_name: Cloud resources are deployed only in approved regions
checks.description: Data residency. For a Saudi customer this is a PDPL question before it is an architecture question, and the approved region list belongs in the assessment scope rather than in this check's defaults.
checks.remediation: Confirm the approved region list with the customer, enforce it with Azure Policy, and migrate or document any resource outside it.

checks.check_name: Storage public network access is disabled
checks.description: Public network access on a storage account exposes its endpoint to the internet even when container ACLs are private.
checks.remediation: Set public network access to Disabled and connect through private endpoints.
